   -------------
   -- Reaches --
   -------------

   function Reaches (H : Heap; I, Y : Extended_Index) return Boolean is
     (Y /= 0
      and then (Y = I
                or else (H.Links (Y).Parent /= 0
                         and then Reaches (H, I, H.Links (Y).Parent))))
   with Ghost,
        Pre                => Well_Linked (H)
                              and then I <= H.Count
                              and then Y <= H.Count,
        Subprogram_Variant => (Increases => Size_Of (H, Y));
   --  Y lies in the tree rooted at I. Stated as a walk *up* the parent links
   --  rather than down the child links, which is what makes it well founded
   --  for the same reason Lemma_Above is: a parent holds a strictly larger
   --  subtree, and Extended_Index is bounded above.

   ------------------------
   -- Lemma_Reaches_Child --
   ------------------------

   procedure Lemma_Reaches_Child (H : Heap; I, C, Y : Extended_Index)
     with Ghost,
          Pre  => Well_Linked (H)
                  and then I in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then C in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then Y in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then (C = H.Links (I).Left
                            or else C = H.Links (I).Right)
                  and then Reaches (H, C, Y),
          Post => Reaches (H, I, Y),
          Subprogram_Variant => (Increases => Size_Of (H, Y));
   --  What the tree of a child is part of: the tree of its parent. This is
   --  the one step that lets the frame lemma below recurse into a subtree.

   procedure Lemma_Reaches_Child (H : Heap; I, C, Y : Extended_Index) is
   begin
      if Y = C then

         --  C points back at I, so one step up from C reaches I.

         pragma Assert (H.Links (C).Parent = I);
      else
         Lemma_Reaches_Child (H, I, C, H.Links (Y).Parent);
      end if;
   end Lemma_Reaches_Child;

   -----------------------
   -- Lemma_Model_Frame --
   -----------------------

   procedure Lemma_Model_Frame (H1, H2 : Heap; I : Extended_Index)
     with Ghost,
          Pre  => Well_Linked (H1)
                  and then Well_Linked (H2)
                  and then H1.Count = H2.Count
                  and then H1.Capacity = H2.Capacity
                  and then I <= H1.Count
                  and then (for all Y in 1 .. H1.Count =>
                              (if Reaches (H1, I, Y)
                               then H2.Keys (Y) = H1.Keys (Y)
                                    and then H2.Links (Y).Left
                                             = H1.Links (Y).Left
                                    and then H2.Links (Y).Right
                                             = H1.Links (Y).Right)),
          Post => Tree_Model (H2, I) = Tree_Model (H1, I),
          Subprogram_Variant => (Decreases => Size_Of (H1, I));
   --  Two pool states that agree on every node of the tree rooted at I give
   --  that tree the same model. Only Keys, Left and Right are required to
   --  agree: Tree_Model never reads a Parent field, so relinking the parent
   --  of a detached subtree is invisible to it.

   procedure Lemma_Model_Frame (H1, H2 : Heap; I : Extended_Index) is
   begin
      if I = 0 then
         return;
      end if;

      for C in 1 .. 2 loop
         declare
            Child : constant Extended_Index :=
              (if C = 1 then H1.Links (I).Left else H1.Links (I).Right);
         begin
            if Child /= 0 then

               --  Everything the recursive call needs about the child's tree
               --  is what this call was told about I's tree, one step down.

               for Y in 1 .. H1.Count loop
                  if Reaches (H1, Child, Y) then
                     Lemma_Reaches_Child (H1, I, Child, Y);
                  end if;

                  pragma Loop_Invariant
                    (for all Z in 1 .. Y =>
                       (if Reaches (H1, Child, Z)
                        then H2.Keys (Z) = H1.Keys (Z)
                             and then H2.Links (Z).Left = H1.Links (Z).Left
                             and then H2.Links (Z).Right = H1.Links (Z).Right));
               end loop;

               Lemma_Model_Frame (H1, H2, Child);
            end if;
         end;

         pragma Loop_Invariant
           (for all D in 1 .. C =>
              (declare
                 Ch : constant Extended_Index :=
                   (if D = 1 then H1.Links (I).Left else H1.Links (I).Right);
               begin
                 Tree_Model (H2, Ch) = Tree_Model (H1, Ch)));
      end loop;

      pragma Assert (Reaches (H1, I, I));
      pragma Assert (H2.Links (I).Left = H1.Links (I).Left);
      pragma Assert (H2.Links (I).Right = H1.Links (I).Right);
      pragma Assert (H2.Keys (I) = H1.Keys (I));
   end Lemma_Model_Frame;

   -- Lemma_Reaches_Size --
   ------------------------

   procedure Lemma_Reaches_Size (H : Heap; I, Y : Extended_Index)
     with Ghost,
          Pre  => Well_Linked (H)
                  and then I in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then Y in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then Reaches (H, I, Y),

   --  rules out a node being inside the subtree of one of its own
   --  descendants, and so what separates the pieces a merge step holds apart.

   procedure Lemma_Reaches_Size (H : Heap; I, Y : Extended_Index) is
   begin
      if Y /= I then
         Lemma_Reaches_Size (H, I, H.Links (Y).Parent);
      end if;
   end Lemma_Reaches_Size;

   --------------------------
   -- Lemma_Reaches_Unique --
   --------------------------

   procedure Lemma_Reaches_Unique (H : Heap; I, J, Y : Extended_Index)
     with Ghost,
          Pre  => Well_Linked (H)
                  and then I in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then J in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then Y in 1 .. H.Count
                  and then H.Links (I).Parent = 0
                  and then H.Links (J).Parent = 0
                  and then Reaches (H, I, Y)
                  and then Reaches (H, J, Y),
          Post => I = J,
          Subprogram_Variant => (Increases => Size_Of (H, Y));

   --  is a single chain, so it cannot end at two different parentless nodes.

   procedure Lemma_Reaches_Unique (H : Heap; I, J, Y : Extended_Index) is
   begin
      if Y = I or else Y = J then

         --  A parentless node is reached only by itself: one step up is not
         --  available, so the other side has to be Y as well.

         pragma Assert (if Y = I then Y = J);
         pragma Assert (if Y = J then Y = I);
      else
         Lemma_Reaches_Unique (H, I, J, H.Links (Y).Parent);
      end if;
   end Lemma_Reaches_Unique;

--
--  SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception
--

--  Leftist heaps sharing one arena.
--
--  Heaps.Leftist exports a Heap that bundles a node pool together with the
--  assertion that the pool holds exactly one tree. That is what makes melding
--  two of them expensive: the two operands live in two disjoint arrays, so one
--  of them has to be copied into the other before its root can be spliced in,
--  and an O(m) copy throws away the O(log n) the structure exists for.
--
--  Here the pool is package state and a heap is a root inside it, so several
--  heaps share one array and a meld is the splice and nothing else. The price
--  is that a heap is no longer a first-class object: there is one arena per
--  instantiation, no array of arenas and no passing one to a subprogram. For a
--  collection of mergeable structures and a benchmark that is the right way
--  round, since the k operands of a k-way meld are k trees in one arena rather
--  than k arenas.
--
--  A tree is named by the index of its root, and a root changes whenever the
--  tree is operated on -- a merge returns one of its two operands as the new
--  root -- so every operation takes its tree as `in out` and the caller keeps
--  the updated name.

--  The model of a tree is *cached*, one multiset per node, rather than defined
--  by recursion over the tree. That is the whole reason this unit's invariant
--  can stay as flat as Heaps.Leftist's. A recursive model reads the entire
--  pool, so every mutation owes a proof that the trees not being touched still
--  have the model they had, and stating that means saying which nodes belong
--  to which tree -- exactly the subtree-level reasoning that PROOF.md reports
--  having avoided. A cached model is a field of a node, so a tree's model is a
--  field of its root, and a mutation that leaves a root alone leaves its model
--  alone for free.
--
--  The cache is maintained by one clause of Valid about one node and its two
--  immediate children, which is the same shape as the clause that maintains
--  Size, and it is maintained by the same three assignments. SPARK has no
--  ghost record components and no ghost parameters of non-ghost subprograms
--  (LRM 6.9(7)), so the cache cannot ride along inside the node or be passed
--  in; ghost package state is the one place it can live, and it is erased at
--  run time like every other ghost object here.

--  The ghost model of these units -- a functional multiset -- cannot
--  reasonably be evaluated at run time. Since the contracts are discharged by
--  proof, run-time checking of them is redundant, so assertions are disabled
--  here whatever the compilation switches say.

pragma Assertion_Policy (Ghost          => Ignore,
                         Pre            => Ignore,
                         Post           => Ignore,
                         Assert         => Ignore,
                         Loop_Invariant => Ignore);

with Heaps.Key_Multisets;

generic
   Capacity : Index;
   --  The number of nodes the arena holds, shared by every tree in it

package Heaps.Leftist_Arena with SPARK_Mode is

   use type Key_Multisets.Multiset;

   subtype Tree is Extended_Index range 0 .. Capacity;
   --  A tree of the arena, named by the index of its root. 0 is the empty
   --  tree, and is a valid value of every operation that takes one.

   ---------------------------
   -- Structural properties --
   ---------------------------

   function Valid return Boolean with Ghost;
   --  The arena is well formed: every node in use is a well formed leftist
   --  node whose cached model agrees with its children's, and every node not
   --  in use is on the free chain.

   function In_Use (I : Index) return Boolean with Ghost;
   --  I holds a node of some tree

   function Is_Root (T : Tree) return Boolean with Ghost;
   --  T names a tree of the arena: either the empty tree, or a node in use
   --  with no parent

   function Model (T : Tree) return Key_Multisets.Multiset with Ghost;
   --  The multiset of the keys held in T. This is a *lookup*, not a scan or a
   --  recursion: the answer is the cache of T's root.

   function Size_Of (T : Tree) return Extended_Index
     with Pre  => Valid and then Is_Root (T),
          Post => (Size_Of'Result = 0) = (T = 0);
   --  The number of nodes in T

   function Room return Extended_Index;
   --  How many more keys the arena can hold, over all its trees together

   function Is_Empty (T : Tree) return Boolean is (T = 0);

   function Is_Minimum (T : Tree; K : Key_Type) return Boolean with Ghost;
   --  K is a lower bound of every key held in T

   ----------------
   -- Operations --
   ----------------

   procedure Clear
     with Post => Valid and Room = Capacity;
   --  Empty the arena. Every tree in it ceases to exist, so every name the
   --  caller holds becomes stale; this is the one operation that invalidates
   --  names it was not given.

   function Peek_Min (T : Tree) return Key_Type
     with Pre => Valid and then Is_Root (T) and then T /= 0;

   procedure Insert (T : in out Tree; K : Key_Type)
     with Pre  => Valid and then Is_Root (T) and then Room >= 1,
          Post => Valid
                  and Is_Root (T)
                  and Room = Room'Old - 1
                  and Size_Of (T) = Size_Of (T)'Old + 1
                  and Model (T) = Key_Multisets.Add (Model (T)'Old, K)

                  --  The other trees of the arena are untouched. With a
                  --  cached model this is one equality per root rather than a
                  --  statement about which nodes belong to which tree.

                  and (for all U in Tree =>
                         (if U /= T'Old and then Is_Root (U)'Old
                          then Is_Root (U)
                               and then Model (U) = Model (U)'Old));

   procedure Extract_Min (T : in out Tree; K : out Key_Type)
     with Pre  => Valid and then Is_Root (T) and then T /= 0,
          Post => Valid
                  and Is_Root (T)
                  and Room = Room'Old + 1
                  and K = Peek_Min (T)'Old
                  and Is_Minimum (T, K)'Old
                  and Model (T)'Old = Key_Multisets.Add (Model (T), K)
                  and (for all U in Tree =>
                         (if U /= T'Old and then Is_Root (U)'Old
                          then Is_Root (U)
                               and then Model (U) = Model (U)'Old));

   procedure Meld (T : in out Tree; U : in out Tree)
     with Pre  => Valid
                  and then Is_Root (T)
                  and then Is_Root (U)
                  and then (if T /= 0 and then U /= 0 then T /= U),
          Post => Valid
                  and Is_Root (T)
                  and U = 0
                  and Room = Room'Old
                  and Model (T) = Model (T)'Old + Model (U)'Old
                  and (for all W in Tree =>
                         (if W /= T'Old
                             and then W /= U'Old
                             and then Is_Root (W)'Old
                          then Is_Root (W)
                               and then Model (W) = Model (W)'Old));
   --  Destructive meld, and the point of the unit: T receives every key of U,
   --  which ceases to exist. No node is allocated, freed or copied -- Room is
